{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Contractor Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review findings — Contractor Services Agreement  

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed a playbook review of the Agreement. Of the eighteen rules assessed, ten clauses are compliant (several at the fallback), six are deviations requiring redlines, and two rules have no usable clause at all.

The commercial architecture of the deal is favourable to us in several important respects: the engagement is task-by-task under Statements of Work with no exclusivity, no minimum commitment, no MFN mechanic and no liquidated damages or early-termination fee; there is no audit right running against us; there is no auto-renewal; and ownership of the Works vests in Company with a perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to embedded Contractor Information.

The risk is concentrated in the protection package. Section 7 is headed "Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor" but contains **no indemnity in either direction**, and Section 5(c)'s non-infringement wording is a bare representation with no defence obligation and no remedy. The liability cap is measured by fees paid for the specific SOW Services and carves out only Paragraph 9, leaving confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement fully capped. There is also no conformance warranty of any kind, no exit or data-return mechanics, and no cyber cover for a Contractor that takes our records, data and system access. Separately, we have no ability to terminate an in-flight engagement for convenience, and governing law (Arizona) with mandatory USA&M arbitration sits outside our accepted list.

Our redlines are targeted and, where the playbook permits, pitched at the fallback rather than the preferred position.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability (cap, mutuality, carve-outs) | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 6 Termination |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 1 Purpose of Engagement |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 6 Termination |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 4 Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 6 Termination |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | § 5 Contractor's Representations and Warranties and Warranty Disclaimer |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 3 Contractor's Compensation |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant (fallback) | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 1 Purpose of Engagement |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | § 7 Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor |

---

## 3. Deviations and gaps — what we changed and why

**INDEMN (critical, missing) — § 7.** Despite the heading, Section 7 contains no indemnity language in either direction, and Section 5(c)'s non-infringement warranty is a bare representation with no defence obligation and no remedy. We have inserted our standard Contractor indemnity covering IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with a standard indemnity procedure.

**LOL-CAP (critical, deviation) — § 7.** The cap is mutual and indirect damages are mutually excluded, but the only carve-out is Paragraph 9 (independent-contractor/tax obligations); the fallback requires carve-outs for confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement. The cap is also measured by fees paid for the specific SOW Services, which on a short task-based engagement can fall well below six months' fees. Our redline sets a 12-month fee basis, adds an Excluded Claims sentence, and confirms our payment obligations sit outside the cap.

**LICENSE (high, deviation) — § 4.** The Contractor Information licence runs to Company alone: affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf are excluded with no mechanism to add them, the licence is not irrevocable, and it is not transferable to a successor (Section 10 restricts assignment). That fails the fallback, which requires affiliates on notice and transferability in an M&A transaction. Our additions are minimal and do not disturb Contractor's ownership of its background IP.

**T4C (high, deviation) — § 6.** The term is evergreen (Section 2), but our convenience right is available only when no Statement of Work is outstanding — in practice, no convenience right at all, which fails the fallback. Contractor's 15-day notice is also well short of the 90 days we require. Our redline gives Company 30 days' convenience termination of the Agreement or any SOW with a prepaid-fee refund, and moves Contractor to 90 days.

**ASSIGN (high, deviation) — § 7.** The consent requirement is mutual and reasonableness-qualified, but there is no carve-out permitting assignment to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger or asset sale, so on its face our internal reorganisations and M&A transactions require Contractor's consent. We have added the affiliate/successor carve-out on written notice and confirmed that a change of control gives Contractor no termination or re-pricing right.

**TRANSITION (medium, missing) — § 6.** Termination addresses only final payment and assignment of works in progress. There is no transition assistance, no obligation to return our data or Confidential Information in a usable format, no timeline and no deletion certification (Section 8 imposes no return obligation either). We have inserted the standard exit paragraph: up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, data return within 30 days in machine-readable format, then certified deletion.

**WARRANTY (medium, deviation) — § 5.** Section 5 provides only knowledge-qualified legal-compliance, authority and non-infringement representations. There is no warranty that the Works conform to the Specifications, no warranty period and no remedy, and implied warranties are disclaimed; the "professional and workmanlike" standard in Section 1(b) is a covenant without a remedy. We have inserted the fallback 90-day conformance warranty with re-performance/repair/replacement/refund, plus a no-malicious-code warranty.

**GOVLAW (medium, deviation) — § 7.** Arizona law is outside our accepted list (New York preferred; Delaware, California or England and Wales as fallback), and disputes are pushed into mandatory USA&M arbitration with no stated seat where we require courts. We have moved governing law and exclusive venue to New York County and, if arbitration is retained, seated it there.

**INSURANCE (low, deviation) — § 7.** Workers' compensation, CGL USD 1M and E&O USD 1M are in place with certificates on request, but there is no cyber/privacy cover even though Contractor obtains our records and data and access to our computer systems (Sections 1(c) and 8). The fallback requires E&O USD 1M plus cyber USD 2M. We have added a single cyber line at the fallback level; the lower E&O and missing CGL aggregate limits are points we would raise but not press.

---

## 4. Points to raise, not deviations

- **§ 4 (IP):** ownership of the Works is conditioned on payment of the relevant invoice, and there is no express Customer Data ownership sentence. Worth raising; neither is a deviation.
- **§ 3(b) (Renewal/pricing):** Contractor may change rates on 30 days' notice with no cap. We would propose the lesser of CPI and 3% as a price-predictability point.
- **§ 7 (Non-solicit):** sits at our fallback (mutual, personnel with direct involvement, 12 months, solicitation not no-hire) but lacks carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches — a drafting request only.
- **§ 4(b)(ii) (Non-compete):** restricts our resale/use of Contractor's own materials; this is a licence-scope point addressed under LICENSE, not a restrictive covenant.

---

## 5. Walk-away items

We should not sign without resolution of the two critical items, which together leave us with no recourse for the risks this engagement actually creates:

1. **No Contractor indemnity anywhere in the document (§ 7; § 5(c) is a bare representation).** A Contractor indemnity for IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct is required.
2. **Liability cap with effectively no carve-outs (§ 7).** Confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement must be uncapped Excluded Claims, and the cap must move off the single-SOW fee basis to 12 months' fees.

These two are linked: an indemnity subject to a single-SOW cap with no carve-out delivers little value, so they should be negotiated as a package.

---

## 6. Next steps

1. Issue the redline to Contractor covering INDEMN, LOL-CAP, LICENSE, T4C, ASSIGN, TRANSITION, WARRANTY, GOVLAW and INSURANCE.
2. Confirm with the business the expected engagement value and duration, so we can test whether the fee-based cap is adequate and support the 12-month basis.
3. Confirm with IT/Security the scope of Contractor's data and system access under Sections 1(c) and 8, to size the cyber cover and support the data-return and deletion mechanics.
4. Flag the § 3(b) uncapped rate-change right to the business owner and confirm whether we press for a CPI/3% collar.
5. Reserve the two walk-away items for principal-level escalation if Contractor resists; hold the remaining medium and low items for a second pass.

*Prepared on the basis of the verified findings supplied; no other terms have been assessed.*"}
